title: New class schrodinger-poisson, negative: self-gravitating wave matter from a random field collapses into one granular halo; a fuel-paid gain heats it into speckle; with kinetic damping a few clumps condense but churn (0 persistent tracks, 0 persistent splits, merge/split ~1)
summary: world.py is 2D Schroedinger-Poisson wave matter (hbar/m = 1, periodic 128^2, split-step Fourier) from a band-limited random field, optionally opened by a gain g Y psi paid from a regrowing fuel Y, a loss sig |psi|^2 psi and a kinetic damping eta lap psi. Conservative (sp0.png, seed 0, G 5e-4): Jeans collapse by t~50 into a few clumps that merge into one granular halo of grid-scale interference by t=200 (no soliton cores resolved). Gain and loss without damping (spAB.png): the field heats into uniform speckle. With damping eta 0.05, g 0.02, sig 0.002, G 1e-3 (spCD.png, packC): a handful of clumps condense and the mass regrows, but labkit finds 0 persistent tracks and 0 persistent splits on seeds 0 and 1 (T=2000; 172 and 191 merges, merge/split 0.98 and 1.09), and matter is flung out along the grid axes in straight jets, which I read as a periodic-box or grid artifact. Damping alone (eta 0.02, no gain) drains the field to nothing.

finding.operator: self-gravity (Poisson potential) acting on a complex wave field, with a fuel-paid gain, cubic loss and kinetic damping
finding.control: conservative arm (no gain, no damping) and damping-only arm, seed 0; packC seeds 0 and 1
finding.result: conservative: one granular halo by t=200; gain without damping: uniform speckle; damped and fed: 6-8 clumps at t=2000, 0 persistent tracks, 0 persistent splits, merge/split 0.98/1.09; damping only: field decays (mass 16384 -> 17)

limits: Four parameter points, one or two seeds each, 128^2 with dx 1: the halo granules sit at the grid scale, so the conservative arm is under-resolved, and the axis-aligned jets in packC suggest a numerical artifact. A proper test of soliton cores needs a finer grid (or smaller kc) and an isotropic damping scheme; I did not try 3D, a sponge boundary or a non-periodic Poisson solver.
